name: Ashiok, Nightmare Weaver
oracle_text:
+2: Exile the top three cards of target opponent's library.
−X: Put a creature card with mana value X exiled with Ashiok onto the battlefield under your control. That creature is a Nightmare in addition to its other types.
−10: Exile all cards from all opponents' hands and graveyards.
blocked_sentences: +2: Exile the top three cards of target opponent's library.

needs.what: exile the top N cards of a (target player's) library while writing the `exiled_by` link to the source, so the planeswalker's later −X can find them with `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}` -- e.g. `link: true` honoured on `look_at_top` with `destination: "exile"` and `objects: {"count": "all"}` (writing `exiled_by` after the move), or a `top: N` selector key usable by the `exile` op over `{"zone": "library", "player": {"target": "t1"}}`. The rest of the card is now expressible: −X is `cost.loyalty_x` + `choose_permanents` over `{zone: exile, controller: any, exiled_with: self, types: [Creature], mana_value: {op: =, value: {x: true}}, count: 1, as: ...}` then `put_onto_battlefield` (controller you) and `add_subtype` Nightmare on that binding; −10 is `exile` over opponents' hands and graveyards.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `look_at_top` exiles the top N but `_move_found` deliberately writes no `exiled_by` (docs/card-dsl.md, `as` section), so `exiled_with: self` matches nothing; its `as` binding lives for one resolution only, while the −X is a later activation. The `exile` op writes the link (`link`/`until_leaves`) but its selector has no way to say 'the top three cards of a library' -- a `count: 3` over a library zone is a player choice, not the top three. Exiling the look_at_top binding a second time with `link` would move exile->exile and fire a spurious zone change.
